title: DPN: detail-preserving network with high resolution representation for efficient segmentation of retinal vessels
venue: Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Humanized Computing
mechanism: Stacked detail-preserving blocks with no downsampling keep full resolution throughout; about 120k parameters.
adaptation: Add a DPN-style full-res branch (8 blocks, 16-32 ch, on the 1-ch input) concatenated into the last U-Net++ decoder node; about +10% compute. Also usable as a structurally different ensemble member.
min_experiment: Arm: house PF + DPN branch; baseline: house PF; CV gridline IoU, crack IoU; also add as 6th member to the 5-seed PF ensemble. Kill if gridline IoU < +0.03, crack IoU n.d., and ensemble crack IoU < +0.005.
evidence: R: comparable accuracy on DRIVE (20 training images), CHASE_DB1, HRF; 20-160x faster than other methods on DRIVE; ~120k params.
prior_overlap: Partly R5 (2x input, n.d. on test crack IoU under house optimizer). R5 did not add a full-res path at native receptive field, did not target gridline, and did not use PF or ensemble diversity.

alt_notes.adaptation: Add a DPN-style full-resolution branch (8 blocks, 16 to 32 ch) on the 1-ch input, concatenated into the house decoder's last block, which in smp likely has no stride-1 skip.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm house PF + DPN branch + raw-image pixel-unshuffle re-injection vs house PF; 5-fold CV gridline IoU, crack IoU; also as a 6th ensemble member. Kill: gridline IoU < +0.03 and crack IoU n.d.; ensemble crack IoU < +0.005. About 15 GPU-h.
